bugs.name: Rejected external asset URL still creates a draft and reserves its tag
bugs.summary: Saving a new draft with external asset URL not-a-url displays an invalid-URL error, but a draft is still created. Correcting the URL or removing the asset and saving with the same tag then fails with “A release with this tag name already exists.” The Releases list already contains the draft.
bugs.expected: Invalid release URLs should prevent draft creation and leave the tag available.
bugs.actual: Saving a new draft with external asset URL not-a-url displays an invalid-URL error, but a draft is still created. Correcting the URL or removing the asset and saving with the same tag then fails with “A release with this tag name already exists.” The Releases list already contains the draft.
reproSteps: Sign in to Forgejo with the fixture account and create a fresh initialized repository.
Open Releases → New release. Enter a unique tag and a nonempty title.
Add an external asset named invalid-asset with URL not-a-url, then click Save draft.
Observe the invalid-URL banner. Keep the same tag, restore the title if necessary, and remove the invalid asset or replace its URL with https://example.com/release-notes.txt.
Click Save draft again. Observe the duplicate-tag error, then open Releases and inspect the already-created Draft entry.

bugs.name: Correcting validation errors can publish a release that was a draft
bugs.summary: After a validation error while editing a draft, Save draft / Publish release are replaced by Update release. Correcting the form and clicking Update release publishes the draft, creating a tag and showing Stable or Pre-release. Reports cover both invalid external asset URLs and empty release titles.
bugs.expected: Correcting a draft validation error should keep the release a draft.
bugs.actual: After a validation error while editing a draft, Save draft / Publish release are replaced by Update release. Correcting the form and clicking Update release publishes the draft, creating a tag and showing Stable or Pre-release. Reports cover both invalid external asset URLs and empty release titles.
reproSteps: Sign in to Forgejo and create a fresh initialized repository.
Create a release with a unique tag and a nonempty title using Save draft. Verify the Draft badge.
Edit the draft, clear its title, and click Save draft. Observe “form.Title cannot be empty.” and the replacement Update release button.
Enter a nonempty title and click Update release.
Return to Releases. Observe that the release has a Stable badge and a tag instead of remaining Draft.

Reported variant: edit a fresh draft, add an external asset with URL not-a-url, and Save draft. After the error, correct/remove the invalid asset and click Update release; the release becomes Stable or Pre-release.

bugs.name: Invalid external asset validation discards the values being corrected
bugs.summary: An invalid external asset URL is rejected, but the returned release form drops the new asset row or restores the previous saved URL. In the new-release flow it also replaces the custom title with the tag. The draft-edit variant loses the draft-specific buttons as well.
bugs.expected: Validation should preserve entered asset URLs and release titles so they can be corrected.
bugs.actual: An invalid external asset URL is rejected, but the returned release form drops the new asset row or restores the previous saved URL. In the new-release flow it also replaces the custom title with the tag. The draft-edit variant loses the draft-specific buttons as well.
reproSteps: Sign in to Forgejo, create a fresh initialized repository, and open Releases → New release.
Enter a unique tag and a distinct title such as External asset validation preservation.
Add external asset external-doc with URL not-a-url and click Save draft.
Observe the invalid-URL banner, missing asset row, and title reset to the tag.

Edit variant: save a fresh draft with an asset at https://example.com/package.zip, edit it, replace that URL with not-a-url, and submit. The validation error quotes the new invalid value while the field reverts to the old valid URL.

bugs.name: Invalid release tag overwrites the entered title
bugs.summary: On the New release form, the visible error says "form.TagName must be a well-formed Git reference name." The Tag name field and the Release title field both visibly contain "bad tag"; the entered title "Invalid tag validation" is gone.
bugs.expected: An invalid tag should leave the separately entered release title intact.
bugs.actual: On the New release form, the visible error says "form.TagName must be a well-formed Git reference name." The Tag name field and the Release title field both visibly contain "bad tag"; the entered title "Invalid tag validation" is gone.
reproSteps: Sign in to Forgejo, create a fresh initialized repository, and open Releases → New release.
Enter bad tag in Tag name and Invalid tag validation in Release title.
Submit using Publish release; another report used Save draft.
Observe “form.TagName must be a well-formed Git reference name.” Both fields now contain bad tag, so the entered title has been lost.

bugs.name: Duplicate-tag validation clears or replaces the new release title
bugs.summary: Submitting a new release with an already-used tag correctly shows a duplicate-tag error, but loses the newly entered title. One report saw it replaced by the tag; another saw a blank title while the tag and description remained.
bugs.expected: A duplicate tag error should preserve the new release title and description.
bugs.actual: Submitting a new release with an already-used tag correctly shows a duplicate-tag error, but loses the newly entered title. One report saw it replaced by the tag; another saw a blank title while the tag and description remained.
reproSteps: Sign in to Forgejo and create a fresh initialized repository.
Create a release or draft with a unique tag such as v0.1.0-dedup-check.
Open New release again. Enter the same tag, a distinct title such as Duplicate tag attempt, and some description text.
Click Save draft. Observe the duplicate-tag banner and inspect the title: it is replaced by the tag or cleared instead of preserving Duplicate tag attempt.

bugs.name: Empty draft-title validation restores the old title and exposes an internal field name
bugs.summary: Submitting an empty title while editing a draft exposes the internal field name `form.Title` and restores the old title in the input.
bugs.expected: An empty title error should be clear and preserve the user’s editable state.
bugs.actual: Submitting an empty title while editing a draft exposes the internal field name `form.Title` and restores the old title in the input.
reproSteps: Create a uniquely tagged draft release in a disposable repository.
Edit the draft, clear its Release title, and submit.
Observe the `form.Title cannot be empty` error and the old title restored in the field.

bugs.name: Draft release byline says released this
bugs.summary: A saved draft release carries a Draft badge but its byline says the author released it.
bugs.expected: The byline should describe creation or saving of a draft, consistent with its Draft status.
bugs.actual: The release list shows a newly saved draft with a Draft badge and “momentic-admin released this” beneath it.
reproSteps: Sign in as a repository owner and open a repository Releases page.
Create a release with a unique tag and title using Save draft.
On the releases list, compare the Draft badge with the “released this” byline.

bugs.name: Older release source archives are hidden by default after adding a newer release
bugs.summary: Adding a newer release or draft collapses Downloads for older published releases, hiding their source ZIP and TAR.GZ links in the release list.
bugs.expected: Every published release with Hide archives unchecked shows its source ZIP and TAR.GZ links in the Releases list, independent of other drafts or releases.
bugs.actual: Only the first listed release defaults to an open Downloads panel. After a newer release or draft is added, older published source archives are hidden in collapsed Downloads panels despite Hide archives being unchecked. Their links remain available by expanding Downloads or opening the release detail page.
reproSteps: Sign in as an owner of an initialized repository with a published release whose Hide archives option is unchecked (tested at momentic-admin/bash-settings-renamed with bash/tag-v1).
Open Releases and verify the published release shows Source code ZIP and TAR.GZ links.
Choose New release, enter a fresh tag and title, target another branch with a different commit if available, and Save draft.

Reload Releases. Observe the older published release has a collapsed Downloads panel and its archive links are initially hidden. Expand Downloads to verify that its ZIP and TAR.GZ links remain available.
Open the published release detail page; both links remain available.

Delete the draft; the older release becomes first and its Downloads opens by default again. Add a newer draft or published release and observe that older Downloads panels default to collapsed, including when commit SHAs differ.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Accepts the initial visibility problem. The source renders the older archive anchors inside collapsed details; this reference does not claim that the links are removed or cannot be shown.
prerequisites: Same archive permission/options for older published release; no injected CSS overriding details.

bugs.name: Invalid tag validation removes the Create tag action
bugs.summary: Submitting an invalid tag through Create tag on the New release form removes the tag-only creation action. Correcting the tag name cannot recover the action without reopening the form.
bugs.expected: Validation preserves Create tag so the user can correct the name and retry tag-only creation.
bugs.actual: Invalid bad tag or bad..tag shows a friendly Git reference validation message, but the response only offers Save draft and Publish release. Correcting the name leaves Create tag absent. Freshly opening the form restores it. Reproduced on two fresh pages with both invalid names.
reproSteps: Sign in as owner of an initialized repository (tested momentic-admin/bash-settings-renamed).
Open Releases → New release.
Enter bad tag (or bad..tag) as the tag name.
Click Create tag and observe the Git reference validation error.
Replace the input with a valid, unused tag name.
Observe Create tag is no longer offered; only Save draft and Publish release remain.
Open New release afresh and observe Create tag is restored.

bugs.name: Whitespace-only release title is accepted and leaves no visible title
bugs.summary: The release form rejects an empty title but accepts a title of only spaces, publishing or saving a release whose title and title link are invisible.
bugs.expected: A whitespace-only title should get the same empty-title validation, or show a visible fallback such as the tag name.
bugs.actual: Three spaces pass validation. The release list and detail page show only the badge, with a blank heading and unnamed link; reopening Edit shows the three-space title persisted.
reproSteps: Sign in as the repository owner and open Releases > New release.
Enter a fresh tag, clear Release title and Publish. Observe Title cannot be empty.
Enter three spaces as the title and Publish (or edit a saved release's title to three spaces and Update).
Observe the release in the list and on its detail page with no visible title or title link.

bugs.name: Filtered tag list paginates by the total tag count and offers empty pages
bugs.summary: Searching Tags for a single match still shows page 2 and Next based on all tags; Next opens an empty list.
bugs.expected: Pagination should reflect the filtered results, as the Releases list does.
bugs.actual: With more than ten tags, a search matching one tag shows that row plus pages 1 and 2 and Next. Next keeps the query and opens page 2 with an empty Tags table.
reproSteps: Sign in as the repository owner and make sure the repository has at least eleven tags (create them with New release > Create tag).
Open Tags and search for one tag's unique name.
Observe one matching row alongside pages 1 and 2 and Next.
Click Next and observe an empty Tags table under the same query.

bugs.name: Mobile Delete release dialog overflows the viewport and clips its confirm button
bugs.summary: At 390 × 844, the Delete release confirmation dialog extends past the right edge of the screen, clipping most of the confirm button.
bugs.expected: The dialog and both of its buttons fit within the mobile viewport.
bugs.actual: The dialog overflows to the right; only a sliver of the confirm button is visible, although clicking it still deletes.
reproSteps: Set the viewport to 390 × 844 and sign in as the repository owner.
Create and publish a disposable release, open it and click Edit.
Click Delete release and observe the confirmation dialog overflowing the right edge.

bugs.name: Delete release does nothing after an edit validation error
bugs.summary: After a release edit fails validation, confirming Delete release closes the dialog but the delete request returns 404 and the release remains.
bugs.expected: Delete release should remove the release, including on the edit page shown after a validation error.
bugs.actual: Clearing the title and clicking Update release shows form.Title cannot be empty. Delete release then opens its confirmation, but Yes closes the dialog with no notice; the delete POST returns 404 and the release still exists. Deleting after a clean reload works.
reproSteps: Sign in as the repository owner and publish a disposable release.
Open its Edit page, clear Release title and click Update release.
After the validation error, click Delete release and confirm Yes.
Observe no deletion or error notice, and the release still listed in Releases.

bugs.name: Deleted release title and notes remain readable at its detail URL
bugs.summary: Deleting a release removes it from the list, but its original title and notes still render at /releases/tag/<tag>; a deleted draft keeps a Draft page with its private notes.
bugs.expected: Deleting a release should remove its title and notes; a remaining Git tag may show a tag-only page without the deleted release's content.
bugs.actual: After deleting a draft or published release, a fresh visit to its tag URL still shows the deleted title and notes (and the Draft badge for drafts), without an Edit control.
reproSteps: Sign in as the repository owner and save a draft release with a fresh tag, a title and notes.
Open its Edit page, click Delete release and confirm.
Verify it disappears from the release list.
Navigate afresh to /<owner>/<repo>/releases/tag/<tag> and observe the deleted title, notes and Draft badge still displayed.
